name: SoundCraft
description: Headless digital audio workstation (SoundCraft from ArtCraft, open source, written in Rust). Imports WAV, MP3, FLAC and OGG audio onto tracks, edits clips — strip silence, trim, separate, move, fades, clip gain — and mixes tracks with volume, pan, EQ, dynamics and reverb plugins and automation through the 480+ commands of the desktop app, bounces the mix to WAV or FLAC with optional peak normalization and encodes it to MP3.
instructions:
SoundCraft runs headless in your own container; every file lives in /work.

1. Upload the user's audio to /work and import it: import_audio {"path":"/work/in.wav"} (WAV, MP3, FLAC, OGG, AIFF) returns the track and clip ids. Pass "track" to put it on an existing track and "at" for its position.
2. Find the command: list_commands {"filter":"silence"} (also "trim", "fade", "gain", "move", "separate", "automation"…). Always pass a filter; never list them all. Each entry tells its params.
3. Run it: execute {"command":"edit.select_all"}, then execute {"command":"edit.strip_silence","params":{"threshold_db":-48}}. Several steps at once go through batch {"calls":[{"command":...,"params":{...}}, ...]}. Undo with execute {"command":"edit.undo"}.
4. Check the result: inspect_session {"detail":"full"} lists the tracks and their clips (id, start, length). Editing keeps the clips where they were, so after strip_silence move the clip to the start: execute {"command":"edit.move_clips","params":{"clips":[<id>],"to":0}}.
5. Export: bounce_mix {"path":"/work/out.wav","normalize":true,"bit_depth":"16","start":0,"end":<length>}. Always pass "end" (the largest clip "end" in inspect_session after the move): without it the whole session length is rendered and removed silence comes back as silence. "normalize" peaks the mix at -0.1 dBFS. FLAC with "format":"flac" and a .flac path. Use a new file name for every export.
6. MP3: encode_mp3 {"path":"/work/out.wav","out":"/work/out.mp3"} ("bitrate_kbps" 32–320, default 192).
7. To continue later: save_session {"path":"/work/<name>.scraft"} and open_session it in a later session.
8. Hand the result over: download it from /work with plugin_download_file.

Positions are samples of the session (48 kHz; imports are resampled) or {"seconds":x}. All paths must be inside /work; relative paths resolve against /work. A new MCP session (e.g. after a reconnect) starts with an empty session, so save .scraft files after each stage and reopen them then. The container and /work are deleted after the conversation is idle, so always download the results.

returns.description: SoundCraft session to continue editing later
